newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First would quarantine tax losses - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ First would quarantine tax losses - Peters.

text.p: Opposition New Zealand First party would quarantine tax losses so they could not be traded between companies within a group, leader Winston Peters said.

Releasing the party's tax policy, Peters said under provisions of a complete rewrite of income tax law, losses would only be used in relation to the business activity that caused the loss if his party won power at the October 12 election.

"A profitable company, able to obtain a tax deduction by making a deduction payment to another conmpany in the group which is in a tax loss situation may be tempted to pour funds into what ultimately is a waste of money.
"If the business of the loss comapny really is worthwhile, it will come into profit and can start deducting the losses itself at that stage," Peters said.
Peters' campaign against corporates' use of the Cook Islands tax haven led to the on-going "winebox" commission of inquiry into the activities of big business and the Inland Revenue Department.
New Zealand First is averaging 15 percent in opinion polls but is likely to hold the balance of power between the incumbent conservative National Party and the opposition parties of the left.

Peters said failing to disclose or falsifying information by a person experienced in tax matters would be a serious offence and for amounts of more than $5 million would carry a maximum penalty of 20 years jail.

Any tax of more than $100,000 evaded by lack of full disclosure would be deemed to have been held in trust for the government and any assets acquired or investment gains made from the use of that money would also belong to the government, Peters said.
A special unit within Inland Revenue under the control of the Police Comissioner would have police powers of search and seizure to investigate and prosecute tax evasion.
Promoting tax schemes designed to produce a commercial gain (including fees) at the expense of the revenue would become a criminal offence.
Reflecting his party's opposition to the surtax on pension income, Peters said New Zealand First would prevent taxes which discriminate on the basis of age.
